name: Massachusetts
summary: A white field with the state arms: a Native American with a bow and arrow on a blue shield, a white star, and an arm holding a broadsword above. The design has been under review by a state commission since 2021.
origin: The flag was adopted in 1908 with the arms on one side and a pine tree on the reverse; since 1971 both sides show the arms.

The arms have been criticised as offensive to Native Americans, particularly the sword raised above the figure. In 2021 the legislature created a commission to recommend a new seal and motto; it presented its recommendations in 2024.

symbols.name: Algonquian figure
symbols.description: A Native American holding a bow and an arrow pointed down.
symbols.meaning: Peace; the arrow pointing down signals peaceful intent.

symbols.name: Star
symbols.meaning: Massachusetts as one of the original thirteen states.

symbols.name: Arm and sword
symbols.description: An arm holding a broadsword above the shield.
symbols.meaning: The motto 'Ense petit placidam sub libertate quietem': By the sword we seek peace, but peace only under liberty.

history.label: Arms on the front, pine tree on the reverse

facts: A state commission has recommended replacing the seal, which would change the flag.
The motto comes from a line attributed to Algernon Sidney.
Massachusetts's naval ensign shows a green pine tree on white.
clues: A white flag with a blue shield showing a Native American and an arm with a sword above.
Its arms are under review after criticism by Native groups.
Its Latin motto speaks of seeking peace by the sword.
